content.title: About
content.content: Meat pizza topping is a blend of selected meats (beef, pork, chicken), spices and tomato sauce used to create a flavorful pizza. It offers a rich meaty taste, aromatic spices and a subtle sweet note from the tomatoes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditional Italian recipes for meat topping use only beef and pork, but modern versions often add chicken or turkey.
The topping is frequently prepared in advance and frozen to preserve flavor and reduce pizza preparation time.
Combining meat with tomato sauce enhances iron absorption from the dish.
In some regions smoked meat is used, giving the pizza a distinctive smoky aroma.
Meat pizza topping can also serve as a base for other dishes such as pasta or casseroles.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Meat provides a complete source of protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Red meat is rich in heme iron, which is more readily absorbed than plant‑based iron.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The topping supplies vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Provides zinc
items.content: Zinc contributes to immune function and wound healing.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: A modest amount of mono‑ and polyunsaturated fats in meat can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: High saturated fat content
items.content: Excessive intake of meat topping may raise cholesterol levels, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Tomato sauce and spices often add salt; people with hypertension should choose low‑sodium versions.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow pathogenic bacteria to develop.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may have an allergy or intolerance to specific types of meat.

items.title: Preservatives in processed mixes
items.content: Ready‑made blends may contain additives; opt for products without artificial ingredients when possible.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Evenly spread the topping over the dough before baking, add it toward the end of cooking to retain juiciness, or use it as a filling for wraps and flatbreads. It can also be reheated in a skillet and served with pasta.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags for up to 2 months. Thaw completely and heat to at least 75 °C before use.
